title: Margins at Ds optima beyond conditional centering and d_psi=1
statement: Determine asymptotic margin behavior outside the audited scalar conditionally centered class. Branch (a), E[S_lambda | shat] != 0, owns the live inhabitation question: DS-STABLE-BASINS-FIXED-POINT-GATE gives a necessary population root equation over all Lloyd-stationary branches, with a kappa-dependent compact tilt bound, but not a converse. Measured mix3 searches find a nondegenerate root near the efficient interval optimum with negligible observed price; they do not prove uniqueness, a model class, or empirical transfer. The immediate task is to state a non-centered law class, prove existence or absence of a nondegenerate root, then determine whether a strict population basin transfers to ordinary finite one-point exchange stability despite O(1/N) boundary-noise move gains. Branches d_psi > 1 and d_lambda >= 2 remain open under their audited cardinality and vector-steering restrictions.
warning: The fixed-point gate is necessary, not sufficient. Numerical root searches are windowed measured evidence, and conditional centering is a population property rather than sample preprocessing.
